title: USPS temporarily stops pension payments amid cash 'crisis'
summary: The U.S. Postal Service has temporarily suspended contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System to conserve cash and preserve liquidity amid an ongoing financial crisis, effective April 10, 2026. The suspension frees approximately $2.5 billion in the current fiscal year. USPS CFO Luke Grossmann stated current and future retirees will face no immediate detrimental impact, and the agency emphasized that legislative action is urgently needed to restore profitability.
key_points: USPS Board of Governors voted to temporarily suspend employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System
Suspension frees approximately $2.5 billion in the current fiscal year ($200 million every two weeks normally)
Employee contributions to the retirement system and Thrift Savings Plan contributions continue uninterrupted
Postmaster General David Steiner projects USPS will run out of cash by 2027 without Congressional intervention
USPS is seeking to raise its statutory debt limit from $15 billion to $34.5 billion
USPS has reported cumulative net losses of $118 billion since 2007
